fullPassage: One evening, Andy was sitting alone in a well-known coffee shop in a quiet town near Venice, Italy. As he enjoyed his coffee and the warm, relaxed atmosphere, an elderly man entered and sat at a nearby table. He called the waiter and said, "Two cups of coffee, one on the wall." Andy watched as he was served a single cup but paid for two. After the elderly man left, the waiter took a small note and pinned it to a wooden wall, which already had several pieces of paper attached. Each read, "A Cup of Coffee." A little while later, two well-dressed women arrived. They ordered three cups, drank only two, and paid for all three. Again, the waiter placed a note on the wall. Andy was curious, but he didn't ask anything, and he paid for his coffee and left. A few days later, Andy returned, still thinking about what he had seen. While he was sipping his drink, a poorly dressed man entered. He quietly sat down, glanced at the wall, and said, "One cup from the wall, please." Without a word, the waiter brought him a coffee, smiling respectfully. The man finished his drink and left without paying. The waiter then removed one of the notes from the wall and tossed it into the bin. Suddenly, Andy understood everything. He had witnessed a silent act of generosity — people buying coffee in advance for those in need. The poor man didn't have to explain his situation or ask for help. He was simply served, like anyone else. Andy was deeply moved by the dignity and kindness shown in that small act. He knew that he would never forget that wall — not because of how it looked, but because of what it represented.

questions.passage: One evening, Andy was sitting alone in a well-known coffee shop in a quiet town near Venice, Italy. As he enjoyed his coffee and the warm, relaxed atmosphere, an elderly man entered and sat at a nearby table. He called the waiter and said, "Two cups of coffee, one on the wall." Andy watched as he was served a single cup but paid for two. After the elderly man left, the waiter took a small note and pinned it to a wooden wall, which already had several pieces of paper attached. Each read, "A Cup of Coffee." A little while later, two well-dressed women arrived. They ordered three cups, drank only two, and paid for all three. Again, the waiter placed a note on the wall. Andy was curious, but he didn't ask anything, and he paid for his coffee and left. A few days later, Andy returned, still thinking about what he had seen. While he was sipping his drink, a poorly dressed man entered. He quietly sat down, glanced at the wall, and said, "One cup from the wall, please." Without a word, the waiter brought him a coffee, smiling respectfully. The man finished his drink and left without paying. The waiter then removed one of the notes from the wall and tossed it into the bin. Suddenly, Andy understood everything. He had witnessed a silent act of generosity — people buying coffee in advance for those in need. The poor man didn't have to explain his situation or ask for help. He was simply served, like anyone else. Andy was deeply moved by the dignity and kindness shown in that small act. He knew that he would never forget that wall — not because of how it looked, but because of what it represented.
